name: Adenocarcinoma of the Anal Canal

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Anal Canal Adenocarcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of adenocarcinoma arising from the anal canal epithelium or anal glands
Imaging evidence (MRI or endoanal ultrasound) showing tumor localized to the anal canal
Presence of characteristic clinical symptoms such as rectal bleeding and anal mass
Exclusion of primary rectal adenocarcinoma extending into the anal canal

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of adenocarcinoma localized to the anal canal with exclusion of rectal origin
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pathology, imaging, and clinical correlation.

laboratory: Anemia on complete blood count due to chronic blood loss
Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) levels in some cases
imaging: MRI pelvis showing tumor confined to anal canal with possible local invasion
Endoanal ultrasound demonstrating tumor depth and involvement
CT scan for regional lymph node and distant metastasis evaluation
genetic: KRAS mutations reported in subset of anal adenocarcinomas
Mismatch repair protein deficiency rare but possible
other: Histopathology showing gland-forming malignant epithelial cells with mucin production
Immunohistochemistry positive for CK20 and CDX2, negative for squamous markers

distinguishingFeatures: Histology showing squamous differentiation rather than glandular
Tumor origin primarily in rectum with downward extension
Imaging shows primary mass centered in rectum

redFlags: Unexplained rectal bleeding persisting beyond 2 weeks
New onset anal ulceration or non-healing lesion
references: National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines on Anal Carcinoma, Version 3.2024
Orphanet: Adenocarcinoma of the Anal Canal (ORPHA:424016)
Comprehensive review of anal canal adenocarcinoma: diagnosis and management, Journal of Gastrointestinal Oncology, 2023
